A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v2 ends after the references despite citing appendices; v3 includes Appendices A–J. This limits comparison of the supplementary experiments and settings.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original unlearning-audit, membership-inference and text-reconstruction experiments on Pythia-1.4b and OPT-1.3b.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original empirical results, and the appendices provide additional numerical results, ablations and reconstructed examples.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 changes TULA-DR's stopping condition from convergence to reaching a maximum iteration count N. The reconstruction objective, regularization and clipping remain unchanged. The added decoding explanation documents an existing step rather than establishing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain SynthPAI-age and SynthPAI-inc classification tasks and the same attack-access scenarios. v3 Appendix A also reports a text-completion check for pretraining exposure. Because v2's referenced dataset appendix is missing, whether this diagnostic task was added cannot be established.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain U-LiRA for auditing and LiRA and ULeaks for relaxed membership inference. Retrain, GA, KL, NPO and TaskVec remain the evaluated unlearning methods. The later appendices introduce no additional comparison method against the proposed attacks.

E3.justification: Shared settings remain unchanged, including model sizes, unlearning ratios, attack metrics and the default 1,000-sample training/single-sample reconstruction setting. v3 specifies a 100-sample, half-prefix completion check and detailed supplementary configurations, but v2's missing appendices prevent determining whether those protocols changed or were merely disclosed.

E4.justification: v3 presents batch-size sensitivity, cosine-versus-Euclidean reconstruction ablations, regularization/clipping ablations and reconstruction examples. v2 already refers to batch experiments, ablations and examples in absent appendices, so their additions or revisions cannot be reliably identified. The earlier status of v3's memory-extraction diagnostic is also unresolved.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix D explicitly reports 100 shadow models, with 85 used for distribution estimation and 15 as tested models. These evaluation-replication counts are unavailable in v2, which gives symbolic counts and refers to its missing appendix. This is additional reporting, not evidence that more runs were performed; confidence intervals and seed details remain unreported.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 are identical, and the original plotted results are retained across v3 Figures 3–6. However, v3 supplies substantial concrete results unavailable in v2: memory extraction, training/test accuracy, additional strict attacks, batch reconstruction, ablations and reconstructed texts in Tables 3–21. This is a substantial expansion of available results, without establishing new experiments or same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The likelihood-ratio formulation and reconstruction, regularization and clipping equations retain their mathematical content. Appendix C spells out previously described unlearning objectives; no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the assertion that unlearning 'inevitably leaks' membership information to introducing leakage risks, and explicitly qualifies the over-70% detection finding as a worst-case result. The abstract, research questions and central conclusions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explains how repeated queries could reveal an unlearning event and expands the justification for classification tasks and synthetic data, including difficulties establishing pretraining membership and the models' release ordering. These refine applicability and methodological interpretation without changing the main conclusions.

D1.justification: v3 makes extensive reproducibility information available where v2 supplies only appendix references: dataset construction thresholds, AdamW training settings, unlearning configurations, shadow-model allocation, attack-classifier hyperparameters and padding conventions. Section 4.3 also explains cosine-based decoding. These are documentation gains, not demonstrated changes to the underlying implementations.

R1.justification: v3 adds an introduction paragraph positioning the study alongside concurrent work, including Huang et al. and Shumailov et al., and cites Zhang et al. on membership-evidence limitations. Additional references identify the SynthPAI source and implementation components. The main related-work discussion remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and dataset rationale receive limited rewriting, decoding and metric explanations are expanded, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added. The principal section sequence and most main-text prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds an opening overview figure, redraws the attack diagram, and splits the two crowded four-panel result figures into larger plots distributed between the main text and appendices, with revised colors, axes and legends. Table 2 becomes full-width, and the supplied appendices add extensive tabular displays.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important deficiency of the supplied v2 PDF: implementation details and supporting analyses repeatedly referenced but absent are now inspectable. Dataset definitions, training and attack settings, ablation evidence and reconstruction examples substantially improve completeness and reproducibility, while redesigned plots improve readability. The shared headline results are unchanged; the gain is in documentation and assessable evidence rather than demonstrated performance improvement.
